 Share Add NBC News to Google Election Day is November 3rd. That's 7 days away. Midterm elections are almost always a referendum on the president and his party — in this case, President Donald Trump, two years into his return to Washington. Much of the national spotlight will be on the fight for Congress. Can Democrats ride cost of living concerns and frustration with the president to majorities in the House and Senate, or do Republicans, aided by a friendly map, successfully make the case for their agenda? But there are critical contests down the ballot in each state, and a number of high-profile races for governor that could have implications for the next presidential election, as well as issues like abortion access and data centers.
 Battle for Control

 Battle for control
 The fight for Congress is playing out largely on Republican-held turf — districts and states that President Trump won in 2024. But historic headwinds and an increasingly gloomy political environment for the president's party have made Democrats optimistic about their ability to win, even in unexpected places.
 Senate
 35 Senate seats are up for election on November 3
 Democrats need a net gain of four seats to win control. To get to a majority, Democrats must win in multiple states that Trump won, some by double digits, in 2024.

 Senate battlegrounds
 To win, Democrats must flip four Republican-held seats and hold their seats in states like Michigan, Georgia and New Hampshire. A loss in any of those states would make the Democrats' path much steeper, though the national party is hopeful about Texas and Alaska, red states that the NBC News Decision Desk ratings suggest are in play.

 How NBC News Projects Races 
 The NBC News Decision Desk provides real-time, accurate election results as soon as they are made available by election officials, and independently analyzes vote tallies to decide when races can be projected. Projecting a winner means that the Decision Desk has determined that the trailing candidates cannot catch the leader and that the leading candidate will win the race. This determination is made through a comprehensive analysis, and the Decision Desk only projects a race when it is certain of the outcome.
 How are votes counted? In the 2026 primaries, vote data will be collected in all 50 states for statewide offices, the House of Representatives, key ballot measures and other races of national interest. The Associated Press provides election results data to NBC News and other major news organizations. Data collection is done through multiple sources on Election Day, with data reporters and interviewers across the country calling in county- and precinct-level results on a timely and rolling basis all day long. Vote data is also collected through state and county websites and feeds.
 How does NBC News ensure accuracy? Vote results are rigorously checked and verified. Part of quality control involves checking that vote data is consistent across sources, and we also compare the vote to past election results to see whether the results look extremely different across multiple past races. All projections are made independently of other outlets.
